# Database migrations

*Generated by `docs/generate-reference.ps1`.* Flyway applies these in order on start-up; a migration is never edited after it has been applied, a new one is added instead.

## V1__init_schema.sql

V1 — MailFlow initial schema
Conventions:
  • All PKs are BIGSERIAL (auto-increment).
  • Timestamps stored as TIMESTAMPTZ (UTC).
  • Soft-delete patterns use deleted_at rather than a boolean flag.
  • JSON columns used for extensible custom fields only.
─── Extensions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
USERS & ROLES

Creates: `roles`, `users`, `user_roles`, `recipient_groups`, `recipients`, `recipient_group_members`, `unsubscribe_list`, `email_templates`, `attachments`, `campaigns`, `campaign_recipients`, `email_logs`, `email_events`, `scheduled_campaigns`

## V2__spring_batch_schema.sql

V2 — Spring Batch metadata tables (PostgreSQL dialect)
Copied from Spring Batch's schema-postgresql.sql and adjusted for our
Flyway-managed schema. Spring is configured with jdbc.initialize-schema=never
so we own this DDL.
Sequences for Spring Batch

V4 — Campaign target groups and recipients join tables

## V5__campaign_only_addresses.sql

V5 — Campaign-only addresses
Lets a campaign email typed or uploaded addresses WITHOUT creating saved
contacts. Additive only: no existing row, column or constraint is removed,
and existing data keeps its meaning.
  • campaign_target_addresses holds a campaign's campaign-only addresses
    (what a draft will send to). Rows are deleted with the campaign.
  • campaign_recipients.recipient_id becomes nullable. A row without a
    recipient delivers to a campaign-only address and carries a snapshot of
    it (email, name, first_name, last_name, company, custom_fields).
    Existing rows keep their recipient_id; their snapshot columns stay NULL.

Creates: `campaign_target_addresses`

## V6__campaign_soft_delete.sql

V6 — Campaign soft delete
Deleting a campaign hides it instead of removing its row. email_logs (the
per-message audit trail), email_events, unsubscribe_list and
scheduled_campaigns reference campaigns without ON DELETE CASCADE, and the
delivery history and unsubscribe entries must be kept, so the row stays.
Additive only: two nullable columns and an index. Existing campaigns keep
deleted_at NULL, which means "not deleted"; no existing row is changed.
  • deleted_at: when the campaign was deleted (NULL for a live campaign).
  • deleted_by: the user who deleted it (NULL when not known).

## V7__campaign_custom_body.sql

V7 — Campaign-wide email body
A campaign can carry its own plain-text email body, written in the New
Campaign form, instead of a template's body. The subject stays in
campaigns.subject.
Additive only: one nullable column. NULL means "use the template's body",
which is what every existing campaign does today, so no existing row changes.
  • custom_body: the campaign's own body (plain text, placeholders such as
    {{FirstName}} allowed). When set, it is sent instead of the template's
    bodies. The API limits it to 100,000 characters.

## V8__organizations.sql

V8 — Organizations (company workspaces)
Every user belongs to one organization, and every recipient, group, template,
campaign, attachment and unsubscribe entry is owned by one. Existing rows are
moved into a "Default" organization, so an existing install keeps working.
Email addresses become unique per organization: two companies may each have
the same contact, and an opt-out applies to the company it was made for.
── Users ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
── Company-owned data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
── Uniqueness per organization ─────────────────────────────────────────────
Constraint names are the PostgreSQL defaults from V1 (<table>_<column>_key).

Creates: `organizations`
